questions.questionText: The SI unit of electrical resistivity is:
questions.solution: Resistivity rho has unit Ohm-m from R = rho*L/A.

questions.questionText: Kirchhoff's junction rule is based on conservation of:
questions.solution: Sum of currents at a junction is zero - conservation of charge.

questions.questionText: Kirchhoff's loop rule is based on conservation of:
questions.solution: Sum of potential differences around a closed loop is zero - conservation of energy.

questions.questionText: Doubling the length of a conductor changes its resistance to:
questions.solution: R = rho*L/A. Doubling L doubles R.

questions.questionText: In a Wheatstone bridge at balance:
questions.solution: Balance condition is P/Q = R/S.

questions.questionText: Drift velocity of electrons is proportional to:
questions.solution: vd = eE*tau/m, directly proportional to E.

questions.questionText: A cell of EMF 2V and internal resistance 1 Ohm connected to 3 Ohm gives current:
Resistivity of a semiconductor with temperature:
questions.solution: More carriers generated at higher T reduces resistivity.

questions.questionText: Terminal voltage of a cell is maximum when:
questions.solution: V = EMF - Ir. Open circuit I=0 so V = EMF.

questions.questionText: Two 6 Ohm resistors in parallel give:
Specific resistance depends on:
questions.solution: Resistivity is intrinsic - depends only on material and temperature.

questions.questionText: Power dissipated in resistor R with current I is:
questions.solution: P = I^2 R.

questions.questionText: A potentiometer measures:
questions.solution: Potentiometer draws no current at null point giving accurate EMF.

questions.questionText: Internal resistance of an ideal voltmeter is:
questions.solution: Ideal voltmeter has infinite resistance to draw no current.

questions.questionText: In a meter bridge balance at 40 cm with R=15 Ohm, the unknown S is:
Mobility of a charge carrier is:
questions.optionA: Drift velocity per unit electric field
questions.solution: Mobility mu = vd/E.

questions.questionText: Cells in series give total EMF:
questions.solution: Series: total EMF = e1 + e2 + ... + en.

questions.questionText: Ohm's law is not obeyed by:
questions.solution: Diode has nonlinear V-I characteristic.

questions.questionText: Current density is:
questions.solution: J = I/A, current per unit cross-sectional area.

questions.questionText: A wire of resistance R stretched to double its length has new resistance:
questions.solution: Volume constant: A halves when L doubles. R' = rho*2L/(A/2) = 4R.

questions.questionText: Relaxation time of electrons decreases with:
questions.solution: Higher T increases collisions reducing relaxation time.

questions.questionText: Maximum current from a cell occurs when:
questions.solution: I = EMF/(R+r) is max when R = 0.

questions.questionText: Electrical conductivity is the reciprocal of:
questions.solution: Conductivity sigma = 1/rho.

questions.questionText: 5 cells of 1.5V and 0.5 Ohm each in series with 5 Ohm external resistance give current:
questions.solution: Total EMF = 7.5V, total R = 5+2.5 = 7.5 Ohm, I = 1 A.

questions.questionText: The colour code Yellow-Violet-Brown-Gold represents:
questions.solution: 4(Yellow) 7(Violet) x10^1(Brown) = 470 Ohm, Gold = 5%.
